name: Utkarsh Yadav
lede: I build generative AI that listens, talks back and draws, and I get it running in real time: on GPU clusters for live shows, and on an 8 GB robot.
intro: Most recently an AI/ML Researcher on CoSTAR at Abertay University. Before that, two years lecturing games and 3D at London Met.
now: Looking for research engineering work in generative AI for creative technology.

selected.title: CharacterPlex
selected.tagline: A full-duplex speech model that stays in character
selected.summary: The team wanted spoken characters that follow a story. I fine-tuned NVIDIA PersonaPlex 7B (built on Moshi) so it plays a character from a character sheet, follows story beats and live director notes, and laughs, sighs or whispers on cue, while keeping the base model’s interruptions and backchannels. I generated the training data, wrote the recipe, trained a LoRA and then a full-parameter model, and built a benchmark to measure what actually changed.

results.label: director-note obedience over the base model
memory reveals when a note asks for one

selected.notes: CharacterBench scores 13 characters with local LLM judges and bootstrap confidence intervals. It also showed where the fine-tune got worse (recalling the user’s name), which I fixed at runtime with a user-memory channel rather than another training run.
selected.hook: A 7B voice model that stays in character and takes direction.

selected.title: PersonaPlex at scale
selected.tagline: Twelve live voice calls on one 48 GB GPU
selected.summary: A speech-to-speech model that answers one caller at a time is a demo, not a service. I put PersonaPlex behind vLLM-Omni so one copy of the weights serves many callers: each caller gets their own paged KV cache and codec state, all live calls advance in one batched GPU step every 80 ms, and a gateway admits, pins and rejects calls. The same setup serves CharacterPlex.

results.label: to first audio with one or two callers
to vLLM-Omni to enable sampling (greedy left the model silent)

selected.hook: One GPU, twelve people talking to it at once.

selected.title: Speech Systems
selected.tagline: Say it on stage, see it on screen
selected.summary: The team was curious what speech-to-speech models could do, so I built an orchestrator in a day that loads Moshi, PersonaPlex, Nemotron VoiceChat and others behind one page, and demoed it the next day. Then I heard about an improv idea: a performer talks into a microphone and the screen draws it. I built that in an evening (Ultravox writes the prompt, FLUX.1-schnell renders it) and over the following week extended it to 3D objects, splat scenes and rigged, animated characters.

results.label: speech end to final picture, p50 (was 1.30 s)
what the whole stack had been pinned to by the Slurm launch, until I found it

selected.hook: Say it on stage and watch it appear: picture, 3D, then a moving character.

selected.title: Soran Labs
selected.tagline: A 3D world model that outputs relightable Gaussian splats
selected.summary: I was brought in to understand and maintain this pipeline, which chains several large generative models (including NVIDIA Lyra) to turn a prompt into a relightable 3D Gaussian splat scene. Within a week I had it running on a smaller server with four 48 GB GPUs by lazy-loading and offloading the models that are not needed at each stage (text encoders, camera-trajectory models) and quantising parts of it. When the original developer left I maintained it, and packaged it into Apptainer containers for deployment on the cluster.

results.label: from first look to running on the smaller server
GPUs, down from the original setup

selected.hook: A world model that grows relightable 3D scenes, squeezed onto smaller GPUs.

selected.title: BMO
selected.tagline: An embodied AI companion, and my MSc thesis
selected.summary: BMO is a companion robot in a 3D-printed case that sees, hears and talks without the cloud, on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. I trained a fusion model with a cross-attention bridge on top of frozen V-JEPA 2 (video) and WavJEPA (audio) encoders, fine-tuned a thinker/speaker language-model pair (LFM2.5-350M and Qwen3-0.6B) steered with directive tokens, and wrote a C++/CUDA engine so full-duplex Moshi runs in real time on the device. The face is a procedural C++/GLSL engine built from signed distance functions.

results.label: per 80 ms audio frame on an 8 GB Jetson (p50)
audio-codec RVQ with fused CUDA kernels

selected.notes: The retrieval work is written up as a paper, “Hearing What You See: Efficient Audio-Visual Retrieval from Frozen Encoders”, under review at ECIR 2027. 155.9M trained parameters sit on 722.5M frozen ones. The paper is careful about its own claims: a residual adapter on ImageBind trained with the same clips closes most of the gap, and an audit found batch-dependent padding had inflated an earlier checkpoint by more than twenty points.

earlier.title: 3D Modelling Showcase
earlier.summary: A collection of my latest 3D modeling work created in Blender. This showcase highlights my skills in creating detailed and realistic 3D assets, focusing on texturing, lighting, and rendering techniques.

earlier.title: Escape room for the SCDM Summer Show
earlier.summary: Led a team of Level 4-6 students to create an interactive escape room for the SCDM Summer Show. Designed a detective mystery case-solving theme, from concept to execution. Project timeline over a two-month.

earlier.title: Phase-Functioned Neural Network (PFNN) in Unreal Engine (Unfinished)
earlier.summary: The project implements Phase-Functioned Neural Network (PFNN) by Daniel Holden (2017) within Unreal Engine to manage complex character animations. The project creates a custom plugin to access third party libraries used in the original paper and to streamline the process of recreating the paper in Unreal Engine. Despite advancements in loading network weights asynchronously and calculating trajectories, two primary challenges persist. First, character mesh often undergoes deformation, significantly impacting the visual quality of animations. Second, trajectory calculation inaccuracies lead to inconsistencies in movement predictions. These core issues currently compromise the efficacy of the system, and addressing them forms the crux of ongoing and future development efforts.

earlier.title: Procedural Animation in Unreal Engine (Update)
earlier.summary: This project is an updated version of the procedural animation system I previously developed in Unreal Engine. It focuses on enhancing the quadruped animation system using the Control Rig system and Full Body IK node. The control rig was refined with improved bone controllers for manipulating the gecko's feet based on external data. Feet positions were calculated using line traces, allowing the gecko to step in an arc onto new positions with greater precision. The Full Body IK node was optimized to calculate bone positions using advanced inverse kinematics algorithms, resulting in even more realistic character animations. A post-process animation blueprint was further enhanced to layer multiple animations, incorporate physical simulations, and adjust body parts dynamically. This updated system demonstrates the power of Unreal Engine's animation tools in creating lifelike and immersive quadruped movements.

earlier.title: Procedural Animation in Unreal Engine
earlier.summary: The project showcases a procedural animation system developed in Unreal Engine, utilizing the Control Rig system and Full Body IK node. The control rig was created with bone controllers for manipulating the gecko's feet based on external data. Feet position was calculated using line traces, allowing the gecko to step in an arc onto new positions. The Full Body IK node calculated bone positions using inverse kinematics algorithms, resulting in realistic character animations. A post-process animation blueprint enhanced believability by layering multiple animations, incorporating physical simulations, and adjusting body parts. This blueprint seamlessly blended animations to create lifelike gecko behavior. The project leverages Unreal Engine's powerful animation tools to achieve dynamic and immersive character movements

earlier.title: Augmented reality Beer Pong Game (Unreal Engine)
earlier.summary: BeerPog Champ is an AR-based game inspired by Beer-Pong. Using motion sensor data, players throw virtual ping-pong balls into cups on a virtual table. The game features a simple menu system and aims to provide fun gameplay.

earlier.title: Gek-Go 3D Puzzle Game
earlier.summary: A DES310 group project, mentored by Rockstar. I worked as the engine and tools programmer for this project, developing the initial traversal mechanic for the beta build. After that I went on to work on the water shader, skybox, butterfly particle effects, animations in unreal engine, and inverse kinematics.

earlier.title: Feed-forward neural network for handwritten digit recognition
earlier.summary: Handwritten digit recognition using the MNIST dataset is based ona feed forward neural network architecture and uses a softmax actiavtion function, It is a shallow neural network with no hidden layers. SFML library is used for GUI. The number 6 and 9 do not get recogenised properly in this version, maybe due to the limited training data provided and lack of hidden layers

earlier.title: Convolutional neural network for image classification
earlier.summary: The project is an image classifier developed using Jupyter Notebook and Python. It utilizes a convolutional neural network trained on the CIFAR-10 dataset. Google Colab is used for dataset loading and model training, while the Keras API enables quick definition of deep learning models. Tkinter graphics library provides a graphical user interface for custom image inputs.

earlier.title: AI Patrol Guard Mechanic Unreal Engine
earlier.summary: Patrol Mechanic is an Unreal Engine project showcasing AI patrol guards. Utilizing behavior trees and task nodes, the guards are programmed to protect predefined paths. They employ sight and hearing senses to detect and respond to the player's presence, initiating a chase if spotted. The project highlights the implementation of multiple AI guards to enhance security and create engaging gameplay scenarios.

earlier.title: 4-Player Networking Racing Game
earlier.summary: A multiplayer game developed using SFML networking API. It features a 4-player racing experience, utilizing TCP protocol for data transfer in a hub-to-client model. Each player sends positional data to the server, which is then directed to the respective clients. The application incorporates a sophisticated quadratic prediction algorithm to improve gameplay. However, due to the choice of positional data transfer, the game experiences lag. Optimizing the transfer model by sending key presses would enable real-time updates of player positions, enhancing the gaming experience.

earlier.title: Multi-threaded Mandelbrot CPU
earlier.summary: Multi-threaded Mandelbrot CPU is a project that utilizes thread pooling to efficiently generate the visually stunning Mandelbrot set. With the help of the SFML graphics library, this project provides a high-performance and visually captivating exploration of fractal mathematics.

earlier.title: Multi-threaded Anagram Finder
earlier.summary: Multi-threaded Anagram Finder is a project that efficiently finds anagrams using two data structures, unordered maps and a binary tree. By leveraging thread pooling, it optimizes the process of generating and searching through all possible permutations of a given word. With its computational ease and comprehensive dictionary, it provides a quick and reliable solution for finding anagrams.

earlier.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion using D3D11 Shaders
earlier.summary: A CMP301 project, uses D3D11 Shaders to render a scene from the cult anime Neon-Genesis Evangelion. Gerstner Wave Equation is used for water simulations. Bloom is applied to both the light sources in the scene including the water.

earlier.title: OpenGL Graveyard Scene
earlier.summary: Graveyard Scene is an OpenGL project that immerses you in a hauntingly beautiful graveyard setting. It features a spooky tree, eerie tombstones, and a captivating cottage at the scene's center. The project demonstrates various techniques such as reflection, lighting, and procedural cylinder generation for a well. Additionally, it incorporates object loading and showcases a dynamic day and night cycle, adding depth and realism to the atmospheric experience.

earlier.title: Carbon Rapture (Godot)
earlier.summary: Carbon Rapture is a game jam entry for the ASGJam focused on carbon capture for climate action. It offers an engaging and educational experience, teaching players about the process of carbon capturing through  interactive gameplay and intuitive mechanics, , promoting awareness and knowledge about this important environmental process.

earlier.title: Loopy Trajectory (Unity)
earlier.summary: Loopy Trajectory is a thrilling game jam creation, with the theme of revolution in mind, it is reminiscent of the sensation 'Getting Over It.' Developed in Unity, the game follows the captivating story of Bob, a stranded spaceship pilot trapped in interstellar space. Players embark on an epic journey, maneuvering through challenging levels by utilizing wormholes to reach home. With an engaging storyline and narrative crafted by me, the game immerses players in Bob's extraordinary quest. The evocative audio design, featuring a narrator delivering memorable quotes like 'Don't hate the player, hate the game,' adds an extra layer of depth to this gripping experience.
